summary: Linked-list teardown: swaps in the temporary vtable off_5AC048, walks the node list whose head is this+0x31C calling each non-terminal node's vtable destructor, frees every node with FreeWrapper_7bcf, zeroes the four list bookkeeping fields at this+0x31C/0x320/0x324/0x328, and finishes by re-running VTableInit on this.

operations.description: Overwrite the this vtable pointer (this+0) with off_5AC048 (the temporary teardown vtable).
Load the list head this+0x31C as the walk cursor.
Walk the node list from this+0x31C following each node's next pointer at node+4; the body runs while the cursor is non-null.

Per node, read the active-flag byte at node+0xC (packet guard: flag == 0 marks a terminal node); the vtable destructor is invoked only when the flag is non-zero and the node's vtable pointer is non-null.
Invoke the node's vtable destructor, the first entry of the node vtable, with (node, 1).
FreeWrapper_7bcf(node) frees each node after its optional destructor.
Zero the list bookkeeping fields this+0x31C, this+0x320, this+0x324, this+0x328 after the walk (the raw source writes the four fields twice).
Finish with VTableInit(this), which rewrites the vtable pointer; the call target address is not exposed by the packet.
Called by LinkedListDestroyAt0x444 (0047FBD0) and DestructorWithConditionalFree_ca30 (0048CA30) when the list must be released.
